scope.q: What specific types of clinical notes (e.g., SOAP, progress notes, discharge summaries) are currently consuming the most evening time, and what is their typical structure?
scope.why: Understanding the note types and their required structure directly informs the data extraction and generation model's complexity and output format.

scope.q: What are the primary input modalities currently used for note creation (e.g., dictation, free-text typing, structured templates, in-person scribes), and what systems capture this data?
scope.why: Knowing the current input methods is critical for designing the initial data capture mechanism and integrating with existing clinical workflows.

scope.q: What is the exact workflow for 'clinician approval,' including the average time spent on review, common types of edits made, and the current method for final sign-off into the EHR?
scope.why: Defining the approval process precisely is essential for building an efficient human-in-the-loop system that actually saves time and ensures data integrity.

decomposition.title: Clinical Encounter Data Capture
decomposition.why: This subproblem focuses on reliably acquiring the raw, unstructured information from patient interactions that forms the basis of the notes.

decomposition.title: Clinical Information Extraction & Structuring
decomposition.why: This involves transforming raw data into structured, machine-readable clinical concepts and relationships, which is crucial for accurate note generation.

decomposition.title: Automated Note Drafting Engine
decomposition.why: This component is responsible for generating a comprehensive, contextually relevant draft note from the structured clinical information.

decomposition.title: Clinician Review & Approval Workflow
decomposition.why: This subproblem designs and implements the user interface and backend logic for doctors to efficiently review, edit, and formally approve the drafted notes.

decomposition.title: EHR Read/Write Integration
decomposition.why: Seamlessly exchanging patient context and approved notes with the existing Electronic Health Record system is fundamental for utility and compliance.

components.name: Transcription Service
components.sub: Converts audio to raw text transcripts

components.name: NLP Extraction Service
components.sub: Extracts clinical entities, events, and relations

components.name: EHR Integration Adapter
components.sub: Manages data exchange with the EHR system

components.name: Patient Context DB
components.sub: Stores relevant patient history for note generation

components.name: Note Generation Agent
components.sub: LLM-powered agent to draft clinical notes

components.name: Doctor Review UI
components.sub: Web application for review, editing, and approval

components.name: Audit Logging Service
components.sub: Records all system actions for compliance

sprint.title: Core Data Ingestion & Basic Draft
sprint.deliv: A system that ingests an audio file, transcribes it, extracts basic entities, and outputs a raw, unstructured text draft.

sprint.title: Structured Note Generation & Display
sprint.deliv: The system generates a structured draft note (e.g., SOAP format) from extracted data, displayed in a basic web UI.

sprint.title: Clinician Review & Edit MVP
sprint.deliv: A functional UI where a doctor can view a draft note, make direct text edits, and mark it as 'Approved' (without EHR write-back).

sprint.title: EHR Read Integration for Context
sprint.deliv: The note generation agent can fetch and incorporate specific patient history (e.g., allergies, past diagnoses) from the EHR into the draft.

sprint.title: EHR Write-Back & Audit Trail
sprint.deliv: Approved notes can be successfully written back into the EHR system, and all major actions are logged for auditability.

sprint.title: Error Handling & Robustness
sprint.deliv: Key error scenarios (e.g., transcription failure, EHR write-back error) are handled gracefully with user notifications and retry mechanisms.

sprint.title: Pilot User Acceptance Testing
sprint.deliv: A small group of doctors has successfully used the system end-to-end to generate, approve, and submit at least 10 real clinical notes.

risks.risk: AI-generated notes contain clinically inaccurate or 'hallucinated' information that could lead to medical errors if not caught by the clinician.
risks.mitigation: Implement robust confidence scoring for generated statements, highlight areas of uncertainty for clinician review, and ensure all generated facts are traceable to source data (transcript/EHR).

risks.risk: Integration with the existing EHR system proves more complex or restrictive than anticipated, preventing seamless data exchange.
risks.mitigation: Initiate early technical discussions with the EHR vendor/IT team to understand APIs and data models. Prioritize a minimal viable integration (e.g., direct text entry or simpler HL7/FHIR profiles) for initial deployment.

risks.risk: Clinicians find the review and editing interface cumbersome, or the AI's drafts are consistently poor, leading to increased review time rather than time savings.
risks.mitigation: Involve target clinicians in UI/UX design from the outset, conduct iterative user testing, and implement feedback mechanisms to continuously improve note generation quality and UI efficiency.

risks.risk: Non-compliance with HIPAA or other data privacy regulations due to improper handling, storage, or processing of Protected Health Information (PHI).
risks.mitigation: Architect the solution with PHI security and privacy by design, including end-to-end encryption, strict access controls, regular security audits, and formal compliance reviews with legal counsel.
